question: Point \(A\) on the number line represents \(-2\). Construct a right triangle with legs of lengths 1 and 3. Draw an arc centered at \(A\) with radius equal to the hypotenuse length, intersecting the number line to the right at point \(P\). Approximately what number does \(P\) represent? (Round to 1 decimal place.)
solution: The hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{10}\approx3.162\). Point \(P\) represents \(-2+\sqrt{10}\approx1.162\), which rounds to 1.2 to 1 decimal place.
